worlds.name: Roshar’s sun
worlds.blurb: A large white star, a little smaller than UTol’s. Thirteen planets circle it: three rocky worlds close in, then an asteroid belt, then ten gas giants named with the Vorin numerals.
facts: Ashyn, Roshar, Braize, then ten gas giants
worlds.distText: Placed from the Cosmere star chart (direction only; no distances given)

worlds.name: Ashyn
worlds.status: First planet · the Tranquiline Halls of legend
worlds.blurb: The innermost planet, the world humans came from before Roshar. A global catastrophe, probably from Surges used without restraint, drove most of its people away as refugees. Those who stayed live in floating cities in the sky and a few habitable pockets. The surface is violently volcanic, and the axial tilt gives it seasons. Rosharan myth calls it the Tranquiline Halls.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Roshar
worlds.status: Second planet · Shardworld of Honor, Cultivation and Odium
worlds.blurb: A world of stone and wind scoured by highstorms that roll in from the east every few days. One supercontinent, also called Roshar, holds nearly all its life. Plants pull into the rock when the storm comes, animals carry shells, and spheres left out in a storm fill with Stormlight. The Alethi princes fight an endless war on the Shattered Plains, while old stories speak of Desolations and of the Knights Radiant.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Braize
worlds.blurb: The third rocky planet, cold, barren and swept by wind under a thin atmosphere, probably outside the habitable zone. Rosharans call it Damnation. Its metallic core draws in souls and Investiture, which is why Odium, the Fused and the tormented Heralds were bound here between Desolations.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Jes
worlds.blurb: Jes is one of the ten gas giants beyond the Rosharan asteroid belt, named with the Vorin numerals in order outward from the sun (Jes is one, Ishi is ten). None is habitable, none has known moons or rings, and their faint shadows in Shadesmar suggest no one lives there. Why there are exactly ten, the number Honor holds sacred, is not known. The colour is the one painted on the system chart.
facts: 5th from the sun (1 of the ten gas giants)

worlds.name: Scadrial’s sun
worlds.blurb: Scadrial’s yellow sun. The planet has been moved toward it and back again: the Lord Ruler pushed Scadrial closer, and Harmony later restored it. The system chart shows both the old orbit and the new. Under the ash in the first trilogy the sun looks red.
facts: Scadrial, Aagal Nod, Aagal Uch, two dwarf planets
worlds.distText: Placed from the Cosmere star chart (direction only; no distances given)

worlds.name: Scadrial
worlds.blurb: In the Final Empire, ash falls beneath a red sun. Skaa labor in the fields under the Lord Ruler’s rule, brown-leaved crops struggle to grow, and mists gather as evening falls.
worlds.distText: Illustrative system layout; distances and orbital order are not verified here.

worlds.name: Aagal Nod
worlds.blurb: A blue gas giant with at least six moons, the largest planet in the system. The name comes from the Nelazan people and means Near Eye.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Aagal Uch
worlds.blurb: A red gas giant with at least five moons and a ring system. Its Nelazan name means Far Eye. A comet belt lies beyond it.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Mashe
worlds.blurb: Sel’s sun. Its name holds the Aon Ashe, light.
facts: Donne, Sel, Ky, Ralen, a dwarf planet
worlds.distText: Placed from the Cosmere star chart (direction only; no distances given)

worlds.name: Donne
worlds.blurb: The innermost planet. It lies in the habitable zone but is barren, very hot and scoured by dust storms.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Sel
worlds.status: 2nd from Mashe · Shardworld of Devotion and Dominion
worlds.blurb: Once the city of Elantris shone, and anyone the Shaod took became a near-immortal with silver skin and power drawn from the Aons, the symbols of their writing. Ten years ago it all failed. Now Elantris is a rotting prison where the newly taken are thrown, Arelon is ruled by a merchant king, and the empire of Fjorden, which holds most of the continent, sends priests to convert what is left.
facts: AonDor, drawn from the shape of the land
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Ky
worlds.status: Gas giant · beyond the asteroid belt
worlds.blurb: The first planet past the Selish asteroid belt, apparently a gas giant with four moons. Its other name, Kii, is the Aon for justice.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Ralen
worlds.status: Gas giant · the largest Selish planet
worlds.blurb: Apparently a gas giant, and the largest planet of the system, with five moons and a ring system. A comet belt lies beyond it.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Dwarf planet
worlds.blurb: A small, unnamed dwarf planet just outside the Selish comet belt, at the edge of the system.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Threnody’s sun
worlds.status: Red star of the Threnodite system
worlds.blurb: A red star. In the empty space of this system the Shards Ambition, Odium and probably Mercy fought; Ambition was mortally wounded, and planets that once orbited here were destroyed. The twisted Investiture on Threnody is at least partly a scar of that battle.
worlds.distText: Placed from the Cosmere star chart (direction only; no distances given)

worlds.name: Monody
worlds.blurb: The planet closest to the sun, similar in size to Elegy and Threnody.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Elegy
worlds.blurb: The second planet, with one moon, Coronach.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Threnody
worlds.status: 3rd from the sun · scarred by Ambition’s death
worlds.blurb: A grim frontier world under a red sun. Humans came from the larger continent, now called the Fallen World, where something known only as the Evil appeared long after the Shards left. On the smaller continent the dead linger as shades in the Forests of Hell. Shed blood draws them, and a shade’s touch kills. Silence Montane runs a waystop for travellers and secretly hunts bounties to keep it afloat.
facts: The Fallen World and the forested continent
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Purity
worlds.blurb: The outermost planet, much farther out than the other three and much larger than any of them.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: AisDa
worlds.blurb: The larger star of the Taldain system, a blue-white supergiant, which holds both the Eye of Ridos and Taldain in orbit. Its light is central to how Autonomy Invests the planet.
worlds.distText: Placed from the Cosmere star chart (direction only; no distances given)

worlds.name: The Eye of Ridos
worlds.status: White dwarf behind a particle ring
worlds.blurb: A faint white dwarf wrapped in a dense ring of particles. Every seven orbits of Taldain’s moon it sends pulses of light and Investiture through the ring.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Taldain
worlds.blurb: The only planet of a binary system, held at a Lagrange point between the two stars and tidally locked. Dayside always faces AisDa and is covered in white sand; Darkside always faces the Eye of Ridos, hidden behind its dust. On Dayside the Sand Masters fight with ribbons of sand. After a massacre of the Sand Masters, Kenton believes himself to be the only survivor.
facts: Nizh Da, on a polar orbit over the twilight line
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Drominad
worlds.blurb: The star of First of the Sun, painted pale blue-white on the system chart. Seven planets circle it, named simply by their order: four small worlds in the habitable zone, an asteroid belt, then three gas giants.
facts: First to Seventh of the Sun
worlds.distText: Placed from the Cosmere star chart (direction only; no distances given)

worlds.name: First of the Sun
worlds.blurb: An ocean world with one large mainland and many islands where the Eelakin live. The greatest island, Patji, is a jungle where almost everything can kill you. Trappers like Dusk survive by knowing its rules and by the Aviar, birds that give their owners talents such as seeing danger coming. Now ships from the Ones Above have arrived in orbit. On this globe the Pantheon islands are drawn about five times larger, and the homeisles three times, so they can be seen.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Second of the Sun
worlds.blurb: A habitable-zone world, smaller than First of the Sun, where water is the main surface feature. It may hold fully developed human societies.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Third of the Sun
worlds.blurb: Apparently the smallest planet in the system. It may hold human societies.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Fourth of the Sun
worlds.blurb: The last planet in the habitable zone and the last that might hold fully developed human societies. It appears to have rings. An asteroid belt lies beyond it.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Fifth of the Sun
worlds.blurb: The first gas giant past the asteroid belt, with three major moons and a ring system.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Sixth of the Sun
worlds.blurb: A gas giant with four major moons and a ring system, apparently the largest planet in the Drominad system.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart

worlds.name: Seventh of the Sun
worlds.blurb: The outermost planet, a gas giant with four major moons.
worlds.distText: System drawn enlarged; planet order from the system chart
